svg.title: Dense inner automorphisms and an outer tensor shift
svg.desc: The tracial infinite matrix tensor factor has dense inner automorphisms: each automorphism is implemented exactly on a finite matrix block, and these blocks are dense in trace square norm. Its bilateral tensor shift is outer by a distant-coordinate commutator estimate. Combined with a free ergodic Bernoulli centre shift, this gives an action with no direct unitary correction in its prescribed tensor decomposition. An additional normal fibre-coordinate conjugacy yields a different conclusion.

g.text: Density of inner automorphisms is weaker than innerness
R: the product-trace GNS closure of the matrix tensors M₂(ℂ) over j ∈ ℤ; τ is its faithful normal trace.
Finite blocks control every fixed element
Fₘ = ⊗ⱼ₌₋ₘᵐ M₂(ℂ); Eₘ : R → Fₘ; ‖Eₘ(x) − x‖₂ → 0.
Eₘ is the normal partial-trace map. Eₘ(z) = τ(z)1 for central z, so R is a separable finite factor.
Every automorphism is approximated
Given θ ∈ Aut(R), compare e₁₁ with θ(e₁₁).
Equal trace gives a partial isometry v.
uₘ = Σᵢ θ(eᵢ₁) v e₁ᵢ implements θ on Fₘ.
For m ≥ l: ‖Ad(uₘ)(x) − θ(x)‖₂
GNS unitaries give convergence in predual norm.
One particular shift is outer
σ sends coordinate j to j+1; Pⱼ has trace zero.
Suppose σ = Ad w, and ‖w − Eₘ(w)‖₂ < 1/4.
For j > m+1, Eₘ(w) commutes with Pⱼ.
Then ‖[w,Pⱼ]‖₂ < 1/2.
But ‖σ(Pⱼ) − Pⱼ‖₂ = ‖Pⱼ₊₁ − Pⱼ‖₂ = √2.
Contradiction. Both assertions are proved in Lemma 2B.1.
The direct perturbation obstruction in source Exercise 3
A = L∞(Y,ν), S a free ergodic Bernoulli shift; Γ = ℤ; M = A ⊗̄ R.
(αₙm)(y) = σⁿ(m(S⁻ⁿy)); βₙ shifts only the centre.
If Ad(u₁)α₁ = β₁, then u₁(y)σ(x)u₁(y)* = x for every x ∈ R, almost everywhere.
A countable dense test family gives σ = Ad(u₁(y)*) in one fibre: impossible.
Theorem 2B.2. Even one correcting unitary for the generator is impossible.
With an additional normal fibre-coordinate change Φ, Theorem 3.2 gives Φ⁻¹αᵘΦ = β.
With every fibre automorphism inner, Theorem 3.1 gives the direct correction αᵘ = β.
Full proofs: Lemma 2B.1, Theorems 2B.2 and 3.2; finite cyclic implementers: Exercise 6.7.
Source hypothesis: Takesaki III, XIII.4, Exercises 1 and 3, printed page 79. The closure on Int(R) is retained.
